items.title: Karl Berger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014
items.q: There were not real conductors. ... even Mozart’s time.

ctx.x: Did you avoid the word jazz?

Yeah, yeah. As much as possible. Because you know if I mention the word jazz in a room with 20 people, each of these 20 people have a completely different sound in their head. So this word is no longer functional. It really isn’t. It is functional in the sense that there is a sense of propulsion that you have in world music, which sort of got lost in European music. European music got much more into form and more and more into form, and is being thought of and listened to from the form element and not from the…
The music had a pulse which kept everybody together.
